clue.text: Give comments to an administrative trainee in revolutionary school

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the school's name is read from its end
the trainee is placed inside the school, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
AT is the British civil service abbreviation for an administrative trainee

explanation.surface: A junior civil servant receives feedback while at a radical school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical school, but it only turns the school round. AT for administrative trainee is a British civil-service grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate a text is to add explanatory notes or remarks to it.

clue.text: I will be involved in Capitol manoeuvring almost entirely? Not if this

definitions.text: I will be involved in Capitol manoeuvring almost entirely? Not if this

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so the single letter goes within
manoeuvring moves things about, so the letters of the building's name get rearranged
almost means falling just short, so the last letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written: the seat of the US Congress
all means entirely, wholly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they would be drawn into scheming on Capitol Hill, and the answer: not if they were this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone of this kind would never be caught up in Washington plotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apolitical has no interest in politics, so would never get drawn into Washington scheming.

clue.text: Curve, almost instant indication of circle?

indicators.note: almost stops just short, so the final letter of the word for a moment is cut

parts.note: an arc is a curve
a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A curve that, almost at once, hints at a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK loses its last letter to give TIC. The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the word tells you which circle is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic is the word that specifies one of the Earth's polar circles of latitude, the Arctic Circle.

clue.text: Champion with poster about to appear in election

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster

indicators.note: to appear in something is to show up within it, so this abbreviation goes inside the poll word

parts.note: a vote is an election or ballot
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A campaigner and a poster turn up around election time.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to advocate it, speaking publicly in its support.

clue.text: Hesitate to ignore origin of Welfare State

indicators.note: ignoring the origin of a word means leaving out its first letter, here the first letter of Welfare

parts.note: to waver is to hesitate
the opening letter of Welfare is the one removed

explanation.surface: A government dithers over overlooking how the welfare state began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welfare State' reads as one phrase, but Welfare only supplies the letter to remove and State is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state or assert something firmly as true.

clue.text: Fourteen letters on a line offering no key

parts.note: A to N covers the first fourteen letters of the alphabet
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A short line of text with no key, like a cipher that can't be read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourteen letters' is read literally as the span A to N.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is written without a tonal centre, that is, in no particular key.

clue.text: Web company anger about new source of deception is impressive

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only the first letter of deception is used
about means going around, so the preceding pieces surround the abbreviation for new

parts.note: an ISP is an internet service provider
ire is anger
N is the abbreviation for new
the first letter of deception

explanation.surface: An internet firm's fury at a fresh deceit is quite something.
explanation.walkthrough: The web company and the anger together go around the new letter, so the insertion lands right after the opening I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired work is outstanding, brilliant or impressive.

clue.text: Disagree with European without causing offence

parts.note: to demur is to raise an objection
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Arguing with a fellow European without upsetting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A demure person is modest and reserved, behaving in an inoffensive, unassuming way.

clue.text: Commit to point East when garaging Tesla?

indicators.note: a garage houses a car, so the car's abbreviation is parked inside the other letters

parts.note: a dot is a point
a Tesla is an EV, an electric vehicle
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to point a Tesla eastwards when parking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point East' looks like one direction, but point and East are separate pieces with the car parked between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote time or effort to something is to commit it to that purpose.

clue.text: Selection of candidates left over with operation being put back

indicators.note: putting something back returns it the other way, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A shortlist of applicants remains after a procedure is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left over' looks like one phrase meaning remaining; it is two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a group of people available to choose from, such as a pool of applicants.

clue.text: Musical instrument for us in curiously ambient surroundings

indicators.note: one piece sits in the surroundings, so it goes inside the rearranged letters
something done curiously is done in an odd way, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A musical instrument suited to us in a strangely atmospheric setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surroundings' tells you the rearranged word wraps around the piece for 'for us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a small hand drum with jingling metal discs, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Stratagem? Tense account about it relayed back

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
AC is short for account

indicators.note: something sent back travels the opposite way, so the last pair of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous report of a ploy, passed on back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre to achieve an aim, just as a stratagem is.

clue.text: Describing some memories — a lecturer entering bank?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these pieces are placed within the verb for bank

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
taken as written
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: Remembering past times: a teacher walks into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a noun for a building but is the verb, as in bank on. RE(A DON)LY gives READ-ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Read-only memory (ROM) is computer memory whose contents can be read but not altered.

clue.text: Half of that rift zone is rocky, non-functional

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
half of a four-letter word means keeping just two of its letters, here the front pair

parts.note: the first half of that
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geologist reports that part of a fault zone is unstable and dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' suits a rift zone in the surface but is the anagram signal. On the fritz is American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: On the fritz is US slang for broken or not working properly.

clue.text: Cost of business trip small? That's about $100 too much

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the preceding pieces go round the money figure

parts.note: exes is informal for expenses
S is the abbreviation for small
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, and a C-note is a $100 bill

explanation.surface: A traveller's expenses were small, though the claim was about $100 over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost of business trip' is the informal British word for expenses; 'about' means the expenses-plus-small string goes round the hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess is an amount beyond what is needed or allowed, that is, too much.

clue.text: Most upset with hotel in Swiss resort

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel

explanation.surface: Most guests are annoyed with their hotel at a ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: St Moritz is a famous ski and winter-sports resort in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: Emotionally-charged writer set to return

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: to return is to come back the way you went, so the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A tense author is ready to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Pent-up feelings are held in and bursting to be released, so full of emotional charge.

clue.text: They'll take position on the bridge without recourse to arms

definitions.text: They'll take position on the bridge without recourse to arms

parts.words: They'll take position on the bridge without recourse to arms
parts.note: surface reading: soldiers holding a bridge without fighting
setter's reading: the bridge of the nose, and arms are the side pieces of spectacles that hook over the ears

explanation.surface: Troops occupy a bridge without having to use their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The arms and bridge belong to glasses, not a battle: these spectacles clip on the nose and have no side arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Pince-nez are eyeglasses held on by gripping the bridge of the nose, with no earpieces.

clue.text: Big meal and no drink? Hard to tuck into that

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: tucking something into another thing places it inside, so the hardness letter goes within the drink word

parts.note: a sup is a mouthful of drink
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A feast without drinks is hard to tuck into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' suggests eating, matching big meal, but it signals placing H inside SUP. Nosh-up is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is informal British for a large, satisfying meal.

clue.text: Single male, I will pursue love with love song from Napoli

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the earlier pieces come after the zero letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
sole means single, only
M is the abbreviation for male
taken as written
love again, zero written as O

explanation.surface: A lonely man will chase romance with a Neapolitan love song.
explanation.definitionFit: O Sole Mio is the famous Neapolitan song, written in Naples dialect in 1898.

clue.text: Grape variety in rural area finally overlooked by characters in street maps?

indicators.note: the final letter is overlooked, that is, missed out, at the end of the word for rural area

parts.note: a shire is a county, rural area of England
an A–Z is a British street atlas, named for running from A to Z

explanation.surface: A grape grown in the countryside, ignored by mapmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'overlooked by' fits a piece placed below, but here it pairs with 'finally' for the deletion and 'by' just joins. An A–Z is the classic British city street-map book.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiraz, also called Syrah, is a dark-skinned wine grape.

clue.text: I'll be enthralled by something that makes you go brown

indicators.note: someone enthralled is held captive, so this letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: senna is a laxative, which makes you go to the toilet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a tanning product that turns you brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes you go brown' reads like a suntan, but 'go' is a euphemism and brown is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy reddish- or yellowish-brown pigment and colour.

clue.text: Spray of water from river accepted by famous swimmer

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the river letter goes inside the swimmer's name

parts.note: Mark Spitz won seven Olympic swimming golds in 1972
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A star swimmer is splashed by river water.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritz is a short squirt or spray of liquid.

clue.text: Family newspaper coming back with day featuring legendary hero

parts.note: kin are one's family

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the word for newspaper is read in reverse

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
THUR is short for Thursday

explanation.surface: A family paper returns with a day's special on a mythical champion.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur is the legendary British king of the Round Table.

clue.text: Minor surface damage reduced in Austrian city

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word for surface damage loses its final letter

parts.note: a graze is a light scrape on the surface

explanation.surface: A city in Austria escaped with only light damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Graz is Austria's second-largest city, capital of Styria.

clue.text: Be stunned regarding US city railroad

parts.note: re means regarding, concerning
the El is an elevated urban railway in US cities such as Chicago

explanation.surface: Astonishment about an American city's train line.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or feel dazed, as when shocked or stunned.

clue.text: One knows a vehicle will pass through street

indicators.note: passing through something takes you inside it, so these pieces sit within the street abbreviation

parts.note: St is short for street
taken as written
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone is sure a vehicle will drive down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One knows' reads as a remark but is the definition: someone who knows.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a learned person, someone of great knowledge.

clue.text: US author's penning old rubbish for inert people

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the author's name holds the following pieces

parts.note: Poe's, belonging to Edgar Allan Poe
O is the abbreviation for old
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: An American writer's work contains ancient junk for lazy readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes right after the author's first letter. The definition leans on couch potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes, as in couch potatoes, are idle, sluggish people who barely move.
